NEW DELHI: Domestic inflation data, foreign investor activity, crude oil prices and developments in West Asia are expected to influence stock market sentiment this week. Globally, investors will track US retail sales, Nvidia's earnings and minutes of the Federal Reserve's latest policy meeting for cues on economic growth, interest rates and technology stocks. October wholesale price index (WPI) inflation and merchandise trade data, both scheduled for release on Monday, November 16, will also be among the key domestic indicators. "Movements in crude oil, the dollar, US Treasury yields and FII flows will remain important determinants of market direction. The domestic economic calendar will be busy, with October WPI inflation and merchandise trade data scheduled for Monday, 16 November," Ajit Mishra, SVP - Research at Religare Broking, told PTI. Globally, investors will also monitor US jobless claims and the minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting for signals on the US economy and the likely direction of monetary policy, he added. Siddhartha Khemka, Head of Research, Wealth Management, at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd, said Indian equities could extend their recent gains. "Indian equities are expected to trade with a positive bias this week, extending their gradual upmove. Record buying by foreign institutional investors, strong domestic fundamentals and encouraging second-quarter earnings season support the positive sentiment. "Globally, investors will track Japan's GDP, US retail sales, UK and EU inflation, US jobs data and the Federal Reserve's meeting minutes," he said. Foreign investors made a strong return to Indian equities in the first half of November, investing Rs 84,290 crore after two consecutive months of net outflows. The inflows came amid a global sell-off in AI-related stocks, lower crude oil prices and attractive valuations of large-cap shares. Developments in global markets, particularly volatility in technology stocks, will also influence domestic sentiment, analysts said. Ponmudi R, CEO of online trading and wealth technology firm Enrich Money, said concerns over high artificial intelligence valuations and the sustainability of semiconductor investments had triggered intermittent selling in global technology stocks. "A deeper correction in this segment could dampen broader risk appetite and weigh on sentiment towards Indian IT companies. Investors will also monitor US Treasury yields and the dollar, as further strength in either could tighten financial conditions and influence capital flows into emerging markets," he said.  Crude oil prices and currency movements will remain other important external factors, he added. Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, founder and CEO of research analyst firm HST Wealth, said developments in the US bond market would be important for foreign investment flows. "Strong US retail activity or hawkish signals in the Federal Open Market Committee minutes could reinforce expectations of tighter monetary conditions, keeping Treasury yields above the 5 per cent threshold. Crude oil presents another important variable for domestic sentiment," he said. Indian benchmark indices ended higher last week. The 30-share BSE Sensex gained 564.43 points, or 0.69%, while the 50-share NSE Nifty rose 113.95 points, or 0.45%.
